# Case study — Investigating a legitimate HTTPS connection

**Focus:** Network traffic investigation · Blue Team fundamentals  
**Tools:** Kali Linux 2026.3 · Wireshark 4.6.6 · ping · dig · curl  
**Scope:** Traffic generated by the operator in an authorized lab

## Challenge

Can we reconstruct the key network events of an HTTPS request using packet evidence instead of relying on the application's visible result?

This mini-investigation starts with network reachability and DNS resolution, follows TCP connection setup, examines TLS 1.3 metadata, then checks the TLS certificate and HTTP response with curl.

## Investigation method

1. Captured traffic on the active `eth0` interface using Wireshark.
2. Generated four ICMP Echo Requests to `1.1.1.1` and correlated the corresponding replies.
3. Queried the A record of `microsoft.com` using `dig`.
4. Examined the TCP stream to the IPv4 address returned in the DNS test, and verified SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK.
5. Identified TLS ClientHello, ServerHello and application-data records in the same stream.
6. Used a **separate** `curl -v` HTTPS request to inspect cipher, certificate validation and negotiated HTTP protocol.
7. Issued another HEAD request to obtain the HTTP status code.

## Key findings

| Layer | Finding | Significance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ICMP | Four matched Echo Request / Echo Reply pairs; average observed RTT ~14.63 ms | Confirms ICMP reachability in this test |
| DNS | A-record response for `microsoft.com`; NOERROR; 7.186521 ms | Shows a functioning resolver for this query |
| TCP | Three-way handshake completed on port 443; SYN→SYN-ACK ~13.84 ms | Confirms successful TCP setup |
| TLS | TLS 1.3 ClientHello/ServerHello and encrypted data | Confirms a negotiated encrypted transport in the captured stream |
| Certificate | curl reports hostname match and verify result 0 | Independently verifies certificate acceptance by the local TLS client |
| HTTP | Separate HEAD request received status 301 | Confirms an application-layer response and permanent redirect |

## What this proves — and what it does not

**Demonstrated:** basic protocol analysis, correlation across network layers, readout of connection establishment, TLS metadata interpretation, and disciplined validation of observations.

**Not demonstrated:** detection of malicious behavior, inspection of decrypted HTTPS payloads, full certificate-chain auditing beyond curl's verification result, or identification of the eventual redirect destination.

## Outcome

The controlled investigation reconstructed the network path from a DNS answer to TCP/TLS communication and obtained an HTTP response. The findings are documented in the [full technical report](../reports/network-traffic-report.md), with screenshots deliberately withheld until they can be sanitized.

Add carefully redacted screenshots of the ICMP, DNS, TCP/TLS and curl output. If extending the lab, compare the baseline with a safely generated example of DNS resolution failure or TCP connection refusal.
